questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to study in an English speaking country and in a big city with public transportation and cultural offers.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was really nervous before going to Edinburgh but I'm really glad I did it and despite also being a challenging experience, I ended up having a really good time and enjoying my stay. Edinburgh is a really great city and the University of Edinburgh is a great place to study.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The staff at the Visiting Student Office was really helpful and good at keeping you updated on the exchange and studying process. If you had any questions, the Visiting Student Office was always happy to help.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The first week of the semester was a welcome week, where you had the opportunity to get to know the different offers at the university and get involved in the different societies. There aren't many mandatory events, so it's up to you to seek out the information. Also most of the social events for the Erasmus Society is ticketed and sell out somewhat quickly, so I would recommend buying tickets to these beforehand. Although, I didn't participate in many of the welcome week events, I still felt like I had all the information I needed by just staying updated on the Facebook page for visiting students, the university's website etc. I would recommend downloading the university app to get an overview of the events during the welcome week.

Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was really difficult!! Edinburgh is in a housing crisis and the university is not required to provide student accommodation for Erasmus students only staying one semester, so I had to find housing on my own. When I arrived in Edinburgh, I didn't have a permanent place to stay and it was really stressful. I would recommend future students to start looking for housing as soon as possible. However, I spend months prior to my exchange searching for a place to stay in Edinburgh and I still wasn't able to find anything. I recommend spending a lot of time on the Meadows Share Facebook group and SpareRoom (and maybe consider paying for a premium account to get early bird access because most ads quickly get hundreds of replies).

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Although it's really stressful not having a place to stay when arriving in Edinburgh, I think the best way to go is finding a temporary accommodation (hostels, airbnb etc.) for the first few weeks and then intensely searching while you're actually in Edinburgh. It's really hard to find a place when you're not in the country and there are a lot of scammers. I really struggled with finding a place to stay but I randomly got in contact with some other visiting students who had managed to get a viewing of a flat and needed a extra roommate. It's probably easier as a visiting student just staying for one semester to just rent a room in a flat, but it's not impossible to group together and rent a flat. However, renting a flat can be a hassle as many landlords require a UK guarantor etc, but I think the university in some cases can act as a guarantor? Also don't tell a potential landlord you're are only staying for one semester as most prefer long-term tenants, but most leases in Scotland simply require a 28 days' notice, so it shouldn't be a problem but obviously read the contract beforehand. I recommend contacting The Advice Place at the university for  any questions about housing in Edinburgh and getting them to go over your lease. Also, if you're completely lost keep contacting the student accommodation office at the university and don't take no for an answer as many people did actually end up getting student accommodation this way. Finding housing in Edinburgh is really difficult, but everyone I knew did end up finding a place to stay, so it isn't impossible but I did feel a bit lost and on my own throughout the process. Overall, I really liked living off campus and I was really lucky to find a great place to stay in the city centre with a really nice landlord, but guaranteed student accommodation would have been nice, especially when there's a housing crisis in Edinburgh.

How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The course registration itself was pretty straightforward and the University of Edinburgh guides you through the process. I think it's first come, first served so I recommend sending your application off as soon as possible and be aware of any restrictions from UCPH and the University of Edinburgh by reading the pre-requisites for the courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Yes, the course finder at the university of Edinburgh website, guides and the visiting student office.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the courses however do beware of timetable clashes. Also, I only got my final timetable two weeks into the semester, so I missed the first week of some of my courses but in the end it wasn't really a problem.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I found the registration for courses pretty straightforward and the University of Edinburgh was good at making me aware of course requirements such as how to sign-up for art and design courses. Obviously, take the courses you find interesting but I do recommend reading up on the lecture hours and assessments of the courses you're interested in as I know some visiting students ended up with an overwhelming amount of uni work.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I only ended up taking first and second year courses, so my fellow students were quite young. However, most of courses weren't related to my major at UCPH, so I didn't mind it being at a "lower level" as everything was quite new to me. I think the workload was around the same as UCPH, maybe a bit less and as I had two days off every week where I didn't have any lectures or seminars which I don't have at UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I had lectures which were pretty similar to the lectures at UCPH, but most courses also had seminars which were  discussion based and quite different from the teaching I'm used to. At first, the seminars were a bit intimidating as they required a lot of active participating and speaking, but they are quite useful for asking questions and going more in-depth with the course work and all my teachers were really nice and helpful which made it a bit easier.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Topics in Popular Music
What's Up Doc? Introducing Animation Studies
Creating Edinburgh: The Interdisciplinary City

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed all of my courses. If you want to try something different and want to explore and learn about Edinburgh while studying, I recommend Creating Edinburgh.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The cost of living in Edinburgh is about the same as Copenhagen, however I did find most things a bit cheaper in Edinburgh like groceries and rent. Also, if you live in the city then Edinburgh is a pretty walkable city and you don't really need a monthly bus pass. Also, coffee is a lot of cheaper which was a pleasant surprise.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: See answer above.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are so many societies at the University of Edinburgh, so there are plenty of opportunities for being social and meeting people.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I recommend ESN, the scandi society and the board game society.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I recommend going on trips with ESN and ISTours as these are for visiting students and are somewhat affordable. Scotland is beautiful. I didn't go myself but I heard really good things about Isle of Skye. Also Glasgow is great and very easy to get to by bus or train.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. Edinburgh is not that different from Copenhagen and the Scots are really friendly and polite.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I personally didn't socialize much the local students as I mainly spent my time with other visiting students, but you can definitely  meet local students by getting involved in the societies.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Everyone is really polite, so you will constantly be saying thank you, excuse me and please and you have to queue for the bus and say thank you to the bus driver when you exit.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Edinburgh is a really pretty city and Scotland is so picturesque.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
A bit cliche but: 
Relax - I was really nervous about everything, but it all worked out and everyone I met was really nice. 
Don't spend all your time studying - Obviously, you're there to study but try to also find time to enjoy Edinburgh and explore Scotland.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
If you have any questions or is struggling, just reach out to the University of Edinburgh as they have so many offers and is always eager to help. 
Also, it can get really windy and cold in Scotland so bring warm clothes.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to live in Edinburgh. I really loved it.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Feeling a bit lonely at times and not knowing anybody, but I still had a great time.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No :))

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
